neutrophil.name: Neutrophil
neutrophil.description: The most common white blood cell, with a segmented multi-lobed nucleus (2–5 lobes). Cytoplasm contains fine pinkish granules.
neutrophil.clinicalSignificance: Elevated in bacterial infections, inflammation, and stress. Decreased in viral infections, chemotherapy, or bone marrow failure.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with clinical history and differential white cell count.
nextSteps.flag: Flag if hypersegmented (>5 lobes) — may indicate megaloblastic anaemia.

lymphocyte.name: Lymphocyte
lymphocyte.description: Small, round cell with a large nucleus occupying most of the cell. Scant pale-blue cytoplasm.
lymphocyte.clinicalSignificance: Elevated in viral infections and chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. Low in immunodeficiency states.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with lymphocyte morphology; note any atypical or reactive forms.
nextSteps.flag: Flag if atypical — may indicate viral illness or lymphoma.

monocyte.name: Monocyte
monocyte.description: Large cell with kidney-shaped or horseshoe nucleus. Grey-blue cytoplasm with fine vacuoles.
monocyte.clinicalSignificance: Elevated in chronic infections (TB, SBE), inflammatory conditions, and monocytic leukaemia.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with clinical findings if persistently elevated.

eosinophil.name: Eosinophil
eosinophil.description: Bilobed nucleus with large orange-red granules filling the cytoplasm.
eosinophil.clinicalSignificance: Elevated in allergic conditions, parasitic infections, and eosinophilic disorders.

nextSteps.correlate: Consider parasitic workup if markedly elevated.

basophil.name: Basophil
basophil.description: Large dark-blue to purple granules, often obscuring the bi-lobed nucleus.
basophil.clinicalSignificance: Elevated in myeloproliferative disorders, chronic myeloid leukaemia, and hypersensitivity reactions.

nextSteps.flag: Flag if basophilia is marked — consider haematology referral.

platelet.name: Platelet
platelet.description: Small, anucleate disc-shaped cell fragment. Purple granular appearance on Romanowsky stain.
platelet.clinicalSignificance: Thrombocytopenia indicates bleeding risk; thrombocytosis may occur in reactive states or myeloproliferative disease.

nextSteps.estimate: Estimate platelet count from film if automated count is flagged.
nextSteps.morphology: Note giant platelets or platelet clumps.

erythrocyte.name: Erythrocyte (Red Blood Cell)
erythrocyte.description: Biconcave disc, pale central pallor occupying less than one third of cell diameter. Pink with Wright stain.
erythrocyte.clinicalSignificance: Morphological changes reflect haematological disorders: microcytes in iron deficiency, macrocytes in B12/folate deficiency.

nextSteps.describe: Describe size, shape, and staining characteristics systematically.
nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with MCV and reticulocyte count.

hypersegmentedNeutrophil.name: Hypersegmented Neutrophil
hypersegmentedNeutrophil.description: Neutrophil with 5 or more lobes in the nucleus. Associated with megaloblastic changes.
hypersegmentedNeutrophil.clinicalSignificance: Classic indicator of B12 or folate deficiency. Also seen in iron deficiency and renal failure.

nextSteps.request: Request B12, folate, and reticulocyte count.

blastCell.name: Blast Cell
blastCell.description: Large immature cell with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine chromatin, and prominent nucleolus.
blastCell.clinicalSignificance: Presence of blasts in peripheral blood is a critical finding suggesting acute leukaemia.

nextSteps.urgent: Flag as URGENT. Contact clinical team immediately.

targetCell.name: Target Cell (Codocyte)
targetCell.description: Erythrocyte with a central dense area surrounded by a pale ring and outer dense rim, resembling a shooting target.
targetCell.clinicalSignificance: Seen in haemoglobin C disease, thalassaemia, liver disease, and post-splenectomy.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with haemoglobin electrophoresis and liver function tests.

schistocyte.name: Schistocyte (Fragmented RBC)
schistocyte.description: Helmet-shaped or triangular red cell fragment caused by mechanical destruction.
schistocyte.clinicalSignificance: Indicates microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia (TTP, HUS, DIC).

nextSteps.urgent: Report immediately — associated with life-threatening conditions.
nextSteps.count: Count percentage of schistocytes per 1000 cells.

sickleCell.name: Sickle Cell
sickleCell.description: Crescent or sickle-shaped red cell resulting from HbS polymerisation.
sickleCell.clinicalSignificance: Diagnostic of sickle cell disease (HbSS) or trait in context. Causes vaso-occlusive crises.

nextSteps.confirm: Confirm with haemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC.
nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with reticulocyte count and LDH.

teardropCell.name: Teardrop Cell (Dacrocyte)
teardropCell.description: Pear or teardrop-shaped erythrocyte, often seen with poikilocytosis.
teardropCell.clinicalSignificance: Seen in myelofibrosis, thalassaemia, and infiltrative marrow disorders.

nextSteps.flag: Flag if prominent — consider bone marrow infiltration.

spherocyte.name: Spherocyte
spherocyte.description: Small, dense, spherical red cell lacking central pallor.
spherocyte.clinicalSignificance: Present in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.

nextSteps.request: Request direct Coombs test (DAT) to differentiate causes.

rouleauxFormation.name: Rouleaux Formation
rouleauxFormation.description: Stack of red cells resembling coins, caused by elevated plasma proteins.
rouleauxFormation.clinicalSignificance: Associated with multiple myeloma, chronic infection, and inflammatory conditions. Increases ESR.

nextSteps.protein: Request serum protein electrophoresis if marked rouleaux present.

plasmodiumFalciparum.name: Plasmodium falciparum
plasmodiumFalciparum.description: Ring-form trophozoites: delicate rings, multiple rings per cell, applique positions. No enlarged RBCs.
plasmodiumFalciparum.clinicalSignificance: Most dangerous malaria species. Can cause cerebral malaria, organ failure, and death.

nextSteps.urgent: Notify clinician URGENTLY. Start treatment per protocol.
nextSteps.count: Count percent parasitaemia — greater than 2 percent indicates severe malaria.
nextSteps.speciate: Confirm species on thick and thin films.

plasmodiumVivax.name: Plasmodium vivax
plasmodiumVivax.description: Enlarged, pale, Schuffner-dotted RBCs with amoeboid trophozoites.
plasmodiumVivax.clinicalSignificance: Causes relapsing malaria due to liver hypnozoites. Less severe than P. falciparum but significant morbidity.

nextSteps.report: Report species and stage. Note enlarged RBCs with Schuffner dots.
nextSteps.primaquine: Discuss primaquine for radical cure with clinician.

plasmodiumMalariae.name: Plasmodium malariae
plasmodiumMalariae.description: Band-form trophozoites spanning the RBC diameter. Normal-sized RBCs. Rosette schizonts.
plasmodiumMalariae.clinicalSignificance: Causes quartan (72-hour) fever. Associated with chronic nephrotic syndrome in children.

plasmodiumOvale.name: Plasmodium ovale
plasmodiumOvale.description: Oval, fimbriated (jagged edge) RBCs with Schuffner dots. Fewer merozoites than P. vivax.
plasmodiumOvale.clinicalSignificance: Similar clinical course to P. vivax. Causes relapsing malaria.

nextSteps.differentiate: Differentiate from P. vivax by oval fimbriated RBC morphology.

plasmodiumKnowlesi.name: Plasmodium knowlesi
plasmodiumKnowlesi.description: Morphologically similar to P. malariae in early stages. Found in South and Southeast Asia.
plasmodiumKnowlesi.clinicalSignificance: Zoonotic malaria from macaques. Can cause rapidly progressing severe disease.

nextSteps.pcr: PCR confirmation recommended if P. knowlesi suspected in travellers from SE Asia.

giardiaCyst.name: Giardia lamblia Cyst
giardiaCyst.description: Oval cyst, 8 to 12 micrometres, with 4 nuclei and curved median bodies visible on trichrome stain.
giardiaCyst.clinicalSignificance: Cause of giardiasis — chronic diarrhoea and malabsorption.

nextSteps.stool: Confirm on stool O and P or antigen test.
nextSteps.treat: Metronidazole or tinidazole as per local protocol.

entamoebaHistolytica.name: Entamoeba histolytica Trophozoite
entamoebaHistolytica.description: 12 to 60 micrometre amoeba with a single nucleus, fine peripheral chromatin, and central karyosome. May contain ingested RBCs.
entamoebaHistolytica.clinicalSignificance: Cause of amoebic dysentery and liver abscess.

nextSteps.urgent: Presence of RBCs in trophozoite confirms invasive disease — notify clinician.
nextSteps.serology: Request amoeba serology if liver abscess suspected.

gramPositiveCocci.name: Gram-Positive Cocci
gramPositiveCocci.description: Spherical bacteria retaining crystal violet stain, appearing purple. May appear in clusters (staphylococci) or chains (streptococci).
gramPositiveCocci.clinicalSignificance: Common pathogens include S. aureus, S. pneumoniae, and Enterococcus species.

nextSteps.culture: Report arrangement (clusters, chains, or pairs) and request culture and sensitivity.

gramNegativeRods.name: Gram-Negative Rods
gramNegativeRods.description: Rod-shaped bacteria that lose crystal violet and stain pink or red with safranin counterstain.
gramNegativeRods.clinicalSignificance: Include Enterobacteriaceae (E. coli, Klebsiella), Pseudomonas, and other pathogens.

nextSteps.antibiotic: Notify clinician promptly — empirical antibiotics may be started.

gramPositiveRods.name: Gram-Positive Rods
gramPositiveRods.description: Rod-shaped bacteria retaining purple crystal violet stain.
gramPositiveRods.clinicalSignificance: Include Listeria, Bacillus, Clostridium, Corynebacterium species.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with clinical context (wound, food exposure, etc.).
nextSteps.culture: Culture and spore stain if anthrax or Clostridium suspected.

gramNegativeCocci.name: Gram-Negative Cocci
gramNegativeCocci.description: Spherical bacteria that do not retain crystal violet stain, appearing pink. Often in pairs (diplococci).
gramNegativeCocci.clinicalSignificance: Neisseria gonorrhoeae (STI), Neisseria meningitidis (meningitis), Moraxella catarrhalis (respiratory).

nextSteps.urgent: Intracellular diplococci in CSF — URGENT. Treat for meningococcal meningitis.
nextSteps.culture: Confirm with culture on selective media.

acidFastBacilli.name: Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB)
acidFastBacilli.description: Slender, slightly curved red rods on Ziehl-Neelsen stain against a blue background. Beaded appearance.
acidFastBacilli.clinicalSignificance: Positive AFB smear is presumptive evidence of tuberculosis or other mycobacterial infection.

nextSteps.urgent: Notify clinician and infection control immediately.
nextSteps.culture: Send for mycobacterial culture (MGIT or LJ medium).

hyalineCast.name: Hyaline Cast
hyalineCast.description: Colourless, transparent cylindrical structure. Low refractive index — best seen under reduced light.
hyalineCast.clinicalSignificance: Small numbers are normal, especially after exercise. Increased in dehydration and renal disease.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with clinical history and urine protein.

granularCast.name: Granular Cast
granularCast.description: Cast containing coarse or fine dark granules within the cylindrical matrix.
granularCast.clinicalSignificance: Indicates renal tubular damage or glomerulonephritis.

nextSteps.urgent: Report presence — associated with significant renal pathology.
nextSteps.rft: Correlate with renal function tests and proteinuria.

waxyBroadCast.name: Waxy/Broad Cast
waxyBroadCast.description: Wide, homogeneous, waxy-appearing cast with sharp edges and broken ends.
waxyBroadCast.clinicalSignificance: Indicates severe or chronic renal disease with reduced tubular flow.

nextSteps.urgent: Report immediately — indicates advanced renal failure.

calciumOxalateCrystal.name: Calcium Oxalate Crystal
calciumOxalateCrystal.clinicalSignificance: Common in normal acidic urine; may be increased with oxalate-rich diet. Abundant in ethylene glycol poisoning.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with urine pH and clinical history.
nextSteps.toxicology: If ethylene glycol poisoning suspected, notify clinician URGENTLY.

uricAcidCrystal.name: Uric Acid Crystal
uricAcidCrystal.description: Yellow-brown rhomboid or barrel-shaped crystals. Polarise brightly.
uricAcidCrystal.clinicalSignificance: Found in acidic urine. Associated with gout, high-purine diet, and uric acid stones.

nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with urine pH and serum uric acid.

transitionalEpithelialCell.name: Transitional Epithelial Cell
transitionalEpithelialCell.description: Large, pear-shaped or round cells from the bladder or ureter lining. Larger than renal tubular cells.
transitionalEpithelialCell.clinicalSignificance: Small numbers are normal. Clusters may indicate urothelial carcinoma or catheter trauma.

nextSteps.flag: Flag clusters of transitional cells for cytology referral.
nextSteps.correlate: Correlate with haematuria and clinical symptoms.

pleuralMesothelialCell.name: Pleural Mesothelial Cell
pleuralMesothelialCell.description: Round to oval cells with central nucleus, abundant cytoplasm, and characteristic window between cells in clusters.
pleuralMesothelialCell.clinicalSignificance: Present in pleural effusions. Reactive mesothelial cells are common in benign effusions; malignant transformation must be excluded.

nextSteps.ldh: Correlate with LDH, protein, and glucose (Light's criteria).

lymphocyteFluid.name: Lymphocyte (Body Fluid)
lymphocyteFluid.description: Predominance of small lymphocytes in body fluid — large nucleus occupying most of the cell.
lymphocyteFluid.clinicalSignificance: Predominant lymphocytes in pleural fluid suggest tuberculosis, lymphoma, or chylothorax.

nextSteps.tb: Consider TB work-up: ADA, culture, PCR.

neutrophilFluid.name: Neutrophil (Body Fluid)
neutrophilFluid.description: Segmented neutrophils seen in body fluid, similar morphology to peripheral blood.
neutrophilFluid.clinicalSignificance: Predominant neutrophils suggest acute bacterial infection, parapneumonic effusion, or pancreatitis.

nextSteps.urgent: If ascites or pleural fluid: request culture urgently.
nextSteps.sba: Calculate serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) for ascitic fluid.
